Ligand 1 is the 4-methoxy variant, whose numbering I know: atom 15 is the cap cyclopropane CH bonded to the carbonyl at atom 13 over a non-ring bond, so anchoring there holds the cap constant while I rebuild the azine. I am testing a fluorine at the pyridine C3, which is the one position I have not probed and arguably the most interesting: it sits between the C4 substituent and the bridging N-H, so it is the only place a substituent can perturb the donor itself. A small strongly electron-withdrawing group there should acidify that N-H, which - if the oracle is reading a donor - could either sharpen or spoil the interaction. It is also minimal in size, so unlike the 3-methyl I am testing separately it should not introduce a steric clash with the adjacent amine. Keeping the 4-methyl in place means this is a clean single addition rather than a substitution. Expected product: N-{4-[(3-fluoro-4-methylpyridin-2-yl)amino]phenyl}cyclopropanecarboxamide at about 285 Da.
